acceptance.text: WF UI shows a default-left workspace Explorer that can collapse/float and supports lazy tree browsing, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts, right-click actions, drag/drop, and immediate disk-backed file operations.
Workspace file operations are root-bounded, recorded in a backend operation log, and reversible through the global undo stack with fast delete/restore behavior.
Dragging workspace files/folders, external files, or pasted images into any terminal inserts usable references and stores uploaded files under categorized Harness/user-files directories.

One agent session maps to one PTY; multiple terminal views can observe it, and the active terminal view owns input/resize without breaking existing terminal output, copy/paste, stop/start, or graph controls.

Double-click node settings allow hot editing of role, custom role, prompt/objective, model, provider placeholder, cwd, env, permissions, and launch policy, with restart-required status and restart action for launch-affecting changes.
Trusted built-in component nodes include editable Markdown and Excalidraw-style diagram nodes with backend-owned state, observable inputs/outputs, and agent-readable workflow map context.
CDP/Chrome full-regression validation proves original WF UI functions still work and new flows pass happy-path, edge-case, and UI-display checks with no unexpected console or network failures.

decisions: Pause terminal-input implementation while the broader WF UI product direction is clarified.
Use a fixed-left workspace explorer surface by default, with collapse/floating behavior.
File references and uploads should be accepted by any terminal surface, not only the drawer terminal.
Agent node settings may be edited while a node is live, but changes that affect runtime launch must show restart-required state and provide a restart action.
Explore generic React component nodes and an Excalidraw-like diagram node as first-class workflow map node types, with backend-owned state as the only source of truth.
Workspace Explorer file operations should write to disk immediately and support fast compensating undo via backend event records.
Terminal drop insertion supports both tag and path formats; Shift-drag inserts an absolute path.
Folder references default to @folder(path), with a later context bundle action.
Component nodes start with trusted built-ins, including editable Markdown nodes with WYSIWYG and source modes.
Global undo includes filesystem operations through backend compensating actions.
Terminal input uses one active input owner per PTY session; any terminal can acquire ownership on focus, drag/drop, or paste.
Excalidraw ships first as a dedicated trusted built-in component node before generic third-party component loading.
Markdown nodes initially store backend-owned content under Harness/a2a/component-nodes/.
Use react-complex-tree for the M1 Explorer because it already covers controlled tree behavior, keyboard navigation, multi-select, drag/drop, rename, and accessibility.
Use @mdxeditor/editor for the M3 Markdown node because backend state can remain plain Markdown while the UI supports WYSIWYG and source-oriented editing.
Use @excalidraw/excalidraw for the M3 diagram node as a trusted built-in component backed by backend scene JSON.
Agent nodes gain skill equipment fields: skills, skillPolicy, contextSources, capabilities, role, customRole, prompt, provider, model, cwd, env, permissions, and launchPolicy.
Default node skill assignment is auto-managed by the main agent/control plane from role/task, with user-visible manual override.
Implementation is split into M1 Explorer/terminal context, M2 node settings/skills, M3 trusted component nodes, then final CDP stabilization.
risks: Workspace file references, external file uploads, pasted images, and terminal input are different data paths and should not be collapsed into one mechanism.
Adding file/folder nodes directly to the ReactFlow graph changes the workflow graph model; a fixed explorer panel may satisfy the default-left requirement with lower graph risk.
Custom provider support affects runtime detection, launch arguments, settings persistence, and security boundaries.
Markdown and Excalidraw dependencies add bundle weight and editor integration risk, so they are deferred to M3 after the Explorer/terminal foundation is green.
Recoverable filesystem undo is data-loss sensitive and must be proven with traversal denial, overwrite conflict, stale revision, and large delete tests before UI polish.

M1 backend reviewer found high/medium stability issues in base64 validation, upload bounds, symlink/junction escape protection, arbitrary opId undo safety, trash-source trust, concurrent revisions, Windows reserved filenames, and context-input write ordering; M1 backend is not stable until hardening tests and fixes pass.
